abstract.para: The transactional wrapper has a configuration file, transactional-wrapper.conf, that enables you to switch the functionality off or modify its behavior after performing modifications to the file system.

topic.para: To change the default configuration, copy transactional-wrapper.conf to /etc/.
Modify the file as described in the following sections.

section.title: Disabling the transactional wrapper
section.para: In the file, you can switch off the transactional wrapper by setting the attribute ENABLE_TRANSACTIONAL_WRAPPER to 0:
Keep in mind that this disables calling zypper directly on the immutable system. To perform modifications to the file system, you must use the &tr-up; command.

section.title: Configuring post-transaction behavior
section.para: You can configure what the system does after an operation finishes by changing the value of ACTION. The following values are supported:

listitem.para: This option calls transactional-update apply, and the system switches to the new snapshot with no need to reboot.
The system is rebooted immediately after an operation successfully completes.
A soft reboot is performed immediately after an operation successfully completes.
The system is rebooted immediately using kexec.
This is the default value. The system informs you that a reboot is needed to apply the changes.
